title: Claude Code just got a massive update #claude #tech - YouTube

snippets.text: Anthropic just shipped mods for Claude
code. A few lines of TypeScript and
Claude code shows how full your context
is, stops the delete command before it
runs, and replays every edit it just
made. Hooks could not rewrite events,
draw new UI, or replace built-in
features. Mods can.
Every time Claude code does something,
it emits an event. Calling a tool,
asking for permission, drawing part of
the screen. A mod is one function hooked
into that event, and it can run before
it, after it, or instead of it. The
hooks form a chain, like middleware.
Yours runs, hands the event on, and at
the bottom, Claude code does what it
would have done anyway. Anthropic's
first example is token weather, about 80
lines. A band above the prompt turns
your context window into a forecast. One
small file, clear at 18%. Four big
files, showers at 67. One more, storm at
81%, a signal to wrap up the session.
Blast radius goes further. Ask Claude to
delete the build folder, and the mod
holds the command. It lists the nine
files it would remove, 1.1 megabytes,
and waits. Press two, and Claude gets a
refusal with the reason. Press one, and
the command runs.
Replay theater captures every edit in a
turn. Claude renamed a function across
three files in five edits. Press R, and
a pane steps through each diff, one at a
time.
The bigger change is inside Claude code
itself. Its own {slash} diff pane is now
a mod, and so is the support for
agents.md.
The source sits in the public Claude
code repo. Anthropic plans to move more
built-in features to mods, so you can
strip Claude code down to a small core,
and add back only what you want.
Describe the mod you want, and Claude
writes it, installs it, and hot reloads
it into your session. Mods are not
sandboxed from your machine. They run
with the same access as Claude code
itself, and their publisher is not
Anthropic. On team and enterprise plans
and on managed machines, a built-in mod
called sec default loads first and stops
installed mods from overriding your
permission deny rules. Anthropic also
calls blast radius a safety net, not a
permission system. A script that calls
the delete command gets past it. Use
mods for your own readouts and guards
first. Those are worth it today. Skip
the mods from strangers until you've
checked their repo, and keep hard blocks
in permission rules.
Would you install a stranger's mod with
full access to your machine? Yes or no?
